newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pull back on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pull back on profit-taking.

text.p: Argentine stocks snapped a winning streak to close lower for the first time in 10 sessions Wednesday in a normal bout of profit-taking, dealers said.

"The correction was favored by Wall Street," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "It hasn't marred the optimistic mood but it will make players more selective and wary of movements abroad while the local market consolidates."
The blue-chip MerVal index gave back 1.2 percent to 583.14 after advancing 8.4 percent in nine consecutive sessions of gains.
"The MerVal will probably drift between 575-590 between now and options expirations (Tuesday) because settlements will tend to keep a lid on prices," said Napoli.
Floor volume shrank back to its recent daily average of 14.6 million pesos after soaring Tuesday to a four-month high of 28 million on foreign bidding, especially in oil giant YPF.

"It's very possible investors will take advantage of this fall to take new positions," said Dario Lizzano of brokers Rio Valores. "The technical floor of 550-556 seems to offer good support and fundamentals are positive, although we could see some earnings jitters coming up just like in New York."
The market's all-share index shed 1.3 percent in the session, with losers outstripping winners 33 to 15 and 19 stocks closing flat.
Over-the-counter volume totaled 113.6 million pesos compared to 162.5 million Tuesday.
Heaviest main-tier losers were sugar refiner Ledesma, holding company Comercial del Plata and Telecom, which slid 3.1 percent, 3.0 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
YPF, which rallied 3.0 percent Tuesday and drove the market higher, eased 0.6 percent. "There were few YPF sellers today -- the stock is firm," said Napoli.

The only MerVal gainers were carmakers Ciadea and Sevel, which tacked on 1.1 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively, real estate developer Irsa, which grew 0.9 percent, and Bansud bank, up 0.5 percent.
